recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No further FHIR core action is needed for FHIR-7974 unless a future work group decision revisits the broader Provenance.agent.who target-type set.
issue_request: FHIR-7974 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Provenance change request from the 2015 May ballot. It asked to add Organization to the allowed reference types for the Provenance agent reference because the agent type/definition already allowed an organization and omitting Organization from the reference target list was a substantive oversight.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in git-svn commit e858186b98, matching the Jira comment for SVN revision 5868. That commit changed source/provenance/provenance-spreadsheet.xml from Reference(Practitioner|RelatedPerson|Patient|Device) to Reference(Practitioner|RelatedPerson|Patient|Device|Organization) for the then-current Provenance.agent.actor/reference element.
additional_context: The current resource source is build-scoped through the active source/fhir.ini provenance=Provenance entry. The current element name is Provenance.agent.who after later Provenance refactors, and source/provenance/structuredefinition-Provenance.xml includes Organization among the Reference targetProfile values. Later commits added and reordered other allowed target types for the same element but preserved Organization. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later decision or community discussion contradicting the original applied change.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the authoritative current Provenance StructureDefinition already includes Organization as an allowed target for Provenance.agent.who.
